about: Reference clips for Roof Jumps' movement and feel, and (marked `"for": "city"`) for its city: what's in it, not how it's painted. Labels are ours: what is seen, where, by time from the clip's start (s). Moves use the parkour names where they apply; 'ours' maps a segment to the runner's move or state. Clips and frames are never committed: devtools/refs.mjs makes them again into devtools/out/refs/.

clips.author: 梔虚月 (@KYOGETSU_2026)
clips.title: 空間の連続性を検証中
clips.notes: The first reference (Roof Jumps' first slice, before this manifest; URL recovered 2026-11-19). One take, the eye close behind and a little above, wide. A figure drops her bag, runs off along a railed walkway and crosses low crowded rooftops over rails, units and alleys, nearly every leap held arms straight out (a display posture more than a mechanical one), runs along building faces over an alley, then sinks a long way down an alley to the street, lands and turns. Taken from it: the eye, the city's grain, the lightness (the glide). Labelled 2026-11-19 from a 4 fps sheet (times to the quarter second).

clips.author: 𝖐𝖎𝖚 (@kiuzyx)
clips.title: a job that slowly kills you
clips.notes: A city reference, not a movement one: eight slow, high, still-eyed shots of a dense Japanese city at dusk (lyrics laid over them). Studied for what the city has and how it's put together: off-white and beige concrete faces in tight grids of small, warm-lit windows; continuous balcony bands with railings; bundles of pipes run up and across the faces with bends; ladders up the sides; units on balconies and roofs; panel water tanks, railings and frames on the roofs; blade signs and rooftop billboards; rust streaks; utility poles with dense overhead wires; dark pitched tile roofs and a pagoda among the flat concrete; glass towers behind; steep stepped streets, alleys a body wide. Labelled 2026-11-21 from a 1 fps sheet.
